briefing.opening: Hello everyone. I will now begin the Climate Change Daily Briefing for October 26, 2026. Today, I will deliver key climate-related news, ranging from the direct threats posed by the climate crisis to various domestic and international efforts for carbon neutrality and renewable energy transition, and the international community's movements surrounding the upcoming COP31.

sections.title: 🔴 Climate Crisis: Anomalous Signs Shaking the Korean Peninsula
sections.content: Recently, warning signs indicating the severity of climate change have been incessant on the Korean Peninsula. An unprecedented phenomenon occurred in late October, with 'Typhoon Champi, the latest autumn typhoon on record,' moving northward towards the Korean Peninsula [5]. Fortunately, it weakened into an extratropical cyclone in the early hours of the 26th, but strong wind and high wave advisories were issued for Jeju [63]. Furthermore, the phenomenon of 'premature leaf fall,' where leaves drop without changing color, has been observed, demonstrating the unpredictability of climate change [1]. Internationally, an increasing number of countries are losing land due to the dual challenges of sea-level rise and land subsidence, and concerns about this are also being raised domestically [6]. Measures for zoos to cope with extreme heatwaves are insufficient [64], and the impact of climate change on ecosystems and social infrastructure is also gradually expanding, as seen in the worsening mold problems in Chicago area schools due to intensified summer storms [70].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Domestic and International Efforts for Transition to a Carbon-Neutral Society
sections.content: Efforts to transition to a carbon-neutral society in response to the climate crisis are actively underway both domestically and internationally. The South Korean government has established criteria for designating 'Just Transition Special Zones' to mitigate the socioeconomic impact of the carbon-neutral transition [12]. At the local government level, Seogwipo City is urging registration of mileage for the vehicle carbon neutrality point system [13], and Boryeong City citizens are practicing everyday carbon neutrality by cycling [14, 15, 25], thus encouraging citizen participation. In Gangnam-gu, a 'Carbon Neutrality Practice Education' performance sharing session tailored to children's perspectives was successfully concluded [18, 27, 29], and in Jincheon-gun, a lecture on 'Carbon Neutrality in Daily Life' was held [19], demonstrating efforts to improve awareness through education. Corporations are also accelerating their efforts towards carbon neutrality [22, 23], and contributing to the spread of an eco-friendly culture in various ways [17], such as Gwangmyeong City's example of promoting carbon neutrality values through upcycling and donating waste resources [24]. Internationally, climate learning is being transformed into climate action at COP meetings [72], and the importance of education is being emphasized, with climate change response efforts starting in classrooms in the Terengganu region [74].

sections.title: 🌱 Renewable Energy Expansion and Policy Challenges
sections.content: In the renewable energy sector, positive developments are emerging alongside policy challenges. As 'Renewable Energy Day 2026' was designated as the first official commemorative day, numerous institutions and companies, including NH Nonghyup Bank, Enlighten, and Korea Ocean Business Corporation, received commendations from the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment for their contributions to the development of the renewable energy industry [31, 33, 34, 36, 37, 41, 44, 45, 50, 51, 52, 54, 55, 57]. Large-scale renewable energy projects are also actively underway, with Korea South-East Power Co. (KOEN) promoting the construction of a 435MW offshore wind power plant off the coast of Incheon [39, 42, 47, 58]. Furthermore, while the expansion of AI data centers and renewable energy is expected to accelerate the growth of the Energy Storage System (ESS) market [38], Korean companies are also facing pressure to use carbon-free energy due to the 'monopolization' of renewable energy by big tech companies [32]. Meanwhile, concerns have been raised regarding the Yoon Suk-yeol government's significant reduction in the Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) ratio [59], indicating a need for policy attention to maintain the renewable energy industry ecosystem. As a positive international trend, with the opening of the Australian renewable energy market, eight domestic green companies are planning to target this market [60].

sections.title: 🌍 International Community Urges Climate Action Towards COP31
sections.content: Ahead of the upcoming COP31 (UN Climate Change Conference of the Parties), the international community's calls for climate action and discussions are active. Turkey, the host country for COP31, showed positive movement by doubling its solar and wind power generation, but at the same time, it ranked first in Europe for coal power generation, revealing a dual aspect of its climate policy [62]. Amidst this complex situation, the COP31 host country urged NATO member states to spend more on climate change response than on defense, emphasizing the importance of climate finance [71]. The Green Climate Fund Board is scheduled to deliberate on new climate projects ahead of COP31 [73], and the international community's voice is growing louder that climate finance promised at COP31 must be backed by actual funds [67].

briefing.closing: As you have seen in today's briefing, the climate crisis is impacting every aspect of our lives, but at the same time, domestic and international efforts and innovations to overcome it are continuously ongoing. Sustained interest and participation are needed for all these efforts to bear fruit and accelerate a sustainable future. This concludes today's climate briefing.
